title: Platform Architect 30s Flipbook — draft
content:
Purpose:
A one-sheet / flipbook for Platform Architects and Infrastructure leads — give them 30 seconds per slide to understand why Redwood inference is a safer, lower-friction choice than building a homegrown serving stack. Designed for SDR+AE quick prep, solution engineers on pre-call, and field sellers doing rapid technical skims.

Intended audience:
- Platform architects (SaaS, mid-market to enterprise)
- Core infra teams deciding between managed inference vs self-hosted
- Security/compliance reviewers who need quick signals

Structure (each item => one 30s flip):
1) 1-liner & anchor stats
   - "Redwood Inference: predictable latency, lower unit cost, consistent APIs across private/hosted/dedicated"
   - Anchor metrics to add: p50/p95 token latency, typical cost per 1k tokens (hosted vs reserved), mean failover time
   - TODO: insert perf snapshot from Q4 benchmark (SRE/bench team)

2) What they care about (quick bullets)
   - Deterministic tail latency (SLOs)
   - Predictable capacity & burst handling
   - Isolation for regulated data (VPC, on-prem options)

3) How we actually deliver it (ops-friendly language)
   - Smart routing (region/cost/latency policies)
   - Dedicated pools + autoscale policies (reserve vs burst)
   - KV caching + request-aware batching to reduce token cost

4) Deployment decision matrix (short)
   - Web/Mobile product: Hosted API to validate fast
   - Large throughput/steady traffic: Dedicated reserved capacity
   - Regulated data: Private (VPC/on-prem) with KMS/HSM

5) Top 5 technical objections + pithy comebacks
   - "We can build this ourselves": "Yes — but median build time is X months, and ops cost > 2x; Redwood provides pre-verified kernels/quantization profiles and rollout tooling."
   - "Latency will spike with batching": "We configure continuous batching with latency-aware thresholds; show p95 graphs."
   - "We need air-gapped": "Private on-prem package with audit logs and KMS; add checklist."
   - "Model quality regression concerns": "Built-in eval hooks, canary rollouts, and regression alerts tied to prompt sets."
   - "Cost visibility": "Token-level breakdown + per-route dashboards in Redwood Console."

6) Quick ops checklist for PoC (steps sellers/SEs can send to prospect)
   - 1) small test plan + traffic profile (provide template)
   - 2) pick deployment mode + target latency SLOs
   - 3) baseline model/seq length + perf run (bench team assist)
   - 4) enable KV caching, tune batch windows, run 24h smoke
   - 5) rollback/failed-deploy playbook included in RM template

7) Security & compliance short notes
   - Supported logs, retention, KMS integrations, SOC2/ISO pointers (link to security playbook)

8) Call scripts / probing questions (for AE/SE)
   - "What's your current p95 token latency and how often does it spike?"
   - "Do you have steady load or traffic bursts tied to events?"
   - "Where does data need to live (cloud region, VPC, on-prem)?"

9) What success looks like (metrics to promise in a PoC)
   - Achieve target p95 latency within X% of baseline under similar throughput
   - Reduce token cost by >= Y% via batching/caching within first month
   - No regression alerts on canonical prompts during canary rollout

10) Internal notes / TODOs (for deck owner)
   - Pull in SRE p95 graph for r-large-16 at 512 tokens
   - Validate cost delta numbers with finance for Dedicated offer
   - Add short customer quote (platform team) — ask CS for 1-liner
   - Convert to 6-slide deck + printable 1-pager

Speaker notes / quick props:
- Keep it very short; assume buyer is pressed for time
- If conversation drifts to accuracy, pivot to eval hooks and canary gating
- For procurement questions, route to reserved capacity negotiation play (link in artifacts)

Appendix (links to internal references) — include minimal links when sharing externally:
- Technical gating checklist: CONFLUENCE-PLAT-4321
- PoC runbook template: JIRA-OPS-1298
- Demo app for architects: https://github.com/redwood-inference/demo-apps/pull/84

Notes-to-self style: rough, short phrases, expected to iterate. This lives in Drive as the working flipbook; later will become two artifacts: a printed 1-pager + a 6-slide internal deck for SEs.

End of flipbook draft.
